claims.text: Pre-coating tungsten regions with a conformal nanoscale Cu layer by ALD before spark plasma sintering can overcome void formation and phase separation in W–Cu composites.
ALD-pre-coated W–Cu composites will have enhanced thermal transport while preserving mechanical durability under fusion-reactor irradiation conditions.
Conventional powder infiltration or sintering produces heterogeneities in W particles or connected W skeletons surrounded by Cu.
ALD can deposit a uniform nanoscale Cu layer onto W particles or surfaces.
Spark plasma sintering is applicable to tungsten-based powders.
Spark plasma sintering can densify tungsten-based powders while retaining their initial powder microstructure.
The SPS temperature profile can be selected to avoid Cu boiling and W melting.
A nanoscale conformal Cu interlayer on W surfaces will ensure continuous metallic bonding at the W–Cu interface.
The ALD-deposited Cu layer improves wetting and interfacial integration during sintering.
Improved wetting and interfacial integration minimize void formation and phase separation.
Reduced void formation and phase separation promote a uniform W–Cu microstructure.
A more uniform W–Cu microstructure improves heat conduction.
The proposed interfacial structure retains mechanical integrity under irradiation stress.
Relative to direct Cu infiltration, non-pre-coated SPS W particles, or vapor-coated W powders without ALD, ALD-coated W–Cu will have a more uniform microstructure and fewer interfacial voids.
Relative to the named baselines, ALD-coated W–Cu will have higher thermal conductivity and greater mechanical durability.
Vapor-coated W powders can show near-perfect constituent contact while still suffering residual voids and phase-separation problems.
Accelerated irradiation testing can reproduce service conditions typical of fusion-reactor joints.

Failure to obtain a statistically significant reduction in void fraction together with increases in thermal conductivity and mechanical strength relative to the uncoated SPS control would falsify the hypothesis.
